fix(mcp): create McpServer and transport per-request to fix stateless transport reuse error (#2238)

* fix(mcp): create McpServer and transport per-request

The MCP SDK's WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport is a
single-use object — once handleRequest() is called it sets an
internal _hasHandledRequest flag that causes every subsequent
request to throw:

  Error: Stateless transport cannot be reused across requests.
         Create a new transport per request.

Similarly, McpServer.connect() throws on a second call because
the server stores the transport reference and rejects
reconnection.

The previous implementation created both objects as module-level
singletons, meaning only the very first MCP request ever
succeeded. All subsequent requests from VS Code, Claude Desktop,
and other MCP clients returned a 500 error.

The fix is to create a fresh McpServer and transport for every
POST request in stateless mode, which is the pattern recommended
by the MCP SDK for stateless (sessionless) deployments.

JSON Schema allows array syntax for nullable fields (e.g. "type": ["string", "null"]).

JSON Schema nullable objects ("type": ["object", "null"]) and nullable arrays

for array values. Now normalises the type to a list before checking.

Schemas with equivalent nullable types in different order (e.g. ["string", "null"]

detection. Sorting the array alphabetically before joining ensures consistent output.

Follow-up to Codex P1 on PR #2460. My previous fix switched collapse's

which made downstreamNodeIds always empty: every id in expandedNodes is in

channel/consumer nodes orphaned on collapse in message groups.

initialNodes when no stash is present) so only genuinely-new downstream

perf(core): read git history for RSS feeds from one git log walk (#2925)

getGitHistory ran git through shelljs exec once per file, and shelljs
starts a new Node process for every synchronous exec. RSS feeds call it
for every resource, so large catalogs spent minutes starting processes.

The newest commit for every path now comes from one memoised git log
walk, with a per-file fallback for paths missing from it. The oldest
lookup still needs --follow per file, but now runs git directly with
execFileSync, which also stops the file path being parsed by a shell.
